target_customer: Front end developers and design teams building React web apps; free for students and open source, subscription planned for enterprise
problem: Developers recreate designer mockups by hand as UI code, which is slow and lossy.
business_model: Subscription SaaS for enterprise teams, free for students and open source

founders.name: Jared Pochtar
education: Harvard (undergraduate, completed degree while building the company)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says the two founders had internships at companies including Google, Palantir and Dropbox; which founder worked where is not stated.

founders.name: Gabriel Guimaraes
education: Harvard (undergraduate, completed degree while building the company)
founders.background_notes: Same TechCrunch source; internships are attributed to the pair jointly.

exit.reason: The founders said they built the wrong product, closed it and open sourced the code; the web version was to stay up through April 2019.

competitors.name: Adobe Dreamweaver
competitors.what: Earlier visual web design tool that TechCrunch cites as a prior attempt at automating front end work
competitors.traction_then: Long established but not used for React output

technical_complexity.rationale: Inferring layout constraints from mockup geometry to emit flexbox React code is a hard compiler style problem for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: The constraint inference was clever but design tools and larger vendors could add code export.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The founders concluded in their shutdown note that developers could get most benefits by using JSX better; the product was closed and open sourced.

market_need_then: Handoff between design and engineering was a known pain; TechCrunch reported five customers using the product full time in February 2018.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, developer facing posts on Medium and Launch HN.

branding.community_and_virality: Coverage on TechCrunch and a Launch HN post on Medium; the code was later open sourced on GitHub.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear descriptive name and some launch press, but no sourced evidence of community or growth driven by brand.

outcome_analysis: Pagedraw compiled design mockups to React code and raised seed money during Winter 2018, but the founders later concluded they had built the wrong product because developers could get most of the benefit from better JSX. They shut the product down and open sourced it. The failure factors reflect the founders own stated reasoning rather than a sourced market study.
notes: Seed amounts conflict: TechCrunch says 1.3M seed raised while in school; CB Insights lists 120K from Y Combinator dated 2018-03-19 and rests on a single database (its investor page repeats the 1.3M text). They may be different pieces of funding. The CB Insights page could not be fetched directly (403). Shutdown date not stated on the page. Competitor list is limited because Anima and similar tools were seen only on undated comparison pages. Audit fix: the 120K dated 2018-03-19 (CB Insights, W18 batch) is the standard Y Combinator investment and may be part of the same 1.3M that TechCrunch reported on 2018-02-28, so the two entries may double count; the 120K entry is relabeled other and flagged. The TechCrunch article names no investors for the 1.3M seed, so none are added.
